profile.campus: Alliance Gateway, Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas (Meta's Fort Worth data center campus, expanded to five buildings)
profile.address: Alliance Gateway Freeway, Fort Worth, Tarrant County, Texas, 76178
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 3 of 3 mapped in this cluster) is part of Meta's Fort Worth campus in the Alliance Gateway development in Tarrant County, Texas. Facebook broke ground in 2015 with an original plan for three buildings, expanded to five buildings in 2017, and reached more than 2.6 million square feet campus-wide, according to Data Center Dynamics; the campus is notable as a cold-storage facility built to hold posts, photos, and videos rarely accessed by users, one of only four such Facebook/Meta facilities operated worldwide at the time DCD reported on it. Facebook began construction on the final phase in December 2020, targeting completion in 2022, at a total campus investment of about $1.5 billion, including a $200 million addition specifically to expand cold-storage capacity; staffing was reported at over 150 employees during that final phase, rising toward about 200 staff (Meta employees and contractors) once complete. The campus is LEED Gold certified and reported as powered by 100% renewable energy sourced from roughly 200 megawatts of Texas wind power, with on-site diesel generators for backup, per DCD's reporting; a third-party aggregator listing (DataCenterMap, not an operator-confirmed source) separately cites a similar 200 MW figure for the site, which is treated here only as corroboration of the wind-power figure already reported by DCD, not as an independent primary source. Meta's own current fact sheet for the campus reports more than $1.5 billion invested, groundbreaking dated to 2015, roughly 200-plus operational jobs, 1,200 peak skilled-trade construction workers, more than $5.2 million in direct funding to local schools and nonprofits, and participation in a Meta-supported program adding more than 9,000 megawatts of new renewable energy across more than 40 projects statewide in Texas, a regional grid contribution rather than a Fort Worth-specific figure. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact current building count, or per-building square footage for individual Fort Worth structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

reading.body:
Meta's Fort Worth campus spans more than 2.6 million square feet across five buildings in the Alliance Gateway development, completed in final phase by 2022 at a total investment of $1.5 billion. The campus is built and operated as cold storage for data rarely accessed by users, one of only four such facilities Meta operated worldwide at the time of its last major expansion. Meta reports the campus powered by approximately 200 megawatts of Texas wind power with on-site diesel backup, holds LEED Gold certification, and employs over 200 staff.

At an assumed density of 40 kW per rack typical of cold-storage workloads, 200 MW of IT load translates roughly to 5,000 racks. This puts Fort Worth among the largest cold-storage deployments globally and reflects Meta's strategy to co-locate archival capacity with renewable power in Texas. The published power figure does not appear in Meta's own current fact sheet and is drawn from third-party reporting, which limits its weight as an operator claim.

Fort Worth is ranked 19th among Texas facilities with published capacity figures, though Texas itself hosts only 18 facilities with operator-confirmed megawatt data among 133 mapped sites statewide. The state's total published capacity stands at 468 MW across those 18 facilities. The Alliance Gateway corridor has grown into a broader data center cluster since Meta broke ground in 2015, though Meta's campus remains the largest published anchor there.
